name: Hesper
body:
HESPER
CR 2

XP 600
CN Medium fey
Init +1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 11, flat-footed 13 (+1 Dex, +3 natural)
hp 18 (4d6+4)
Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +5
Defensive Abilities reactor sprite; DR 5/cold iron; Immune fire, radiation; Weaknesses vulnerable to cold

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee mutating touch +2 touch (see below)
Special Attacks energy ray
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 2nd; concentration +6)

Constant—detect radiation
At will—mending
1/day—burning hands (DC 15), shocking grasp

STATISTICS

Str 10 (+0), Dex 12 (+1), Con 13 (+1), Int 11 (+0), Wis 12 (+1), Cha 18 (+4)
Base Atk +2; CMB +2; CMD 13
Feats Skill Focus (Disable Device), Technologist
Skills Diplomacy +11, Disable Device +5, Knowledge (engineering) +4, Knowledge (geography) +7, Perception +8, Stealth +8
Languages Common, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Energy Ray (Sp)

As a standard action, you can fire a ray of either fire or electricity at a target within 60 feet. This is a ranged touch attack that deals 1d4 points of damage of the chosen energy type.

Mutating Touch (Su)

A hesper can deliver an enormous dose of radiation with a touch, triggering sudden mutations and pain in living creatures. With a successful melee touch attack against a living creature, a hesper causes the target to sprout tumors that erupt at the beginning of its next turn, causing a random mutation (roll 1d20 on the table below) that persists for 24 hours.

An affected creature can negate this transformation with a successful DC 13 Fortitude saving throw. Once a creature has been affected by a hesper’s mutating touch, it becomes immune to that particular fey’s mutating touch for 24 hours. The save DC is Constitution-based.

d20	Mutation Effect
1	Additional eyes Target gains light blindness and a +4 bonus to sight-based Perception checks
2–3	Autonomous parasite Target takes 1d6 slashing damage as a parasite emerges
4–5	Bioelectric cells Technological items held by the target gain the broken condition for as long as the target holds them
6–7	Claws, spines, or teeth on one limb Target gains a primary natural attack (1d4 piercing damage if Medium), but it takes a –2 penalty to attacks with twohanded weapons
8–9	Glowing tumors Target sheds light as a lantern and takes a –5 penalty to Stealth checks
10	Gills Target gains the amphibious ability, but takes a –2 penalty to Fortitude saving throws
11	Hypertrichosis Target gains a +1 bonus to its AC, but the max Dex bonus of armor it wears decreases by 1
12–13	Musk gland Target gains a 30-foot aura that nauseates living creatures within it (Fortitude DC 10 + 1/2 the target’s HD + the target’s Con modifier)
14–15	Secondary ears Target gains vulnerability to sonic damage and a +4 bonus to hearing-based Perception checks
16–17	Vestigial limb Target grows a useless extra limb that imparts a –2 penalty to Dex-based skill checks
18–19	Weeping sores Target takes a –2 penalty to Charisma-based skill checks 20 Wracking pain Target is sickened
Reactor Sprite (Su)

If a hesper spends 1 hour in close contact with a starship’s power core or another large power source (such as a fusion reactor), it can form a long-term bond. A hesper can merge with its bonded reactor, gaining fast healing 5 while it remains merged. A merged hesper is aware of what happens in the reactor’s immediate vicinity, but if the reactor is broken or suffers the wrecked critical damage condition, the hesper is immediately expelled and takes 3d6 damage. If the reactor is destroyed while the hesper is merged with it, the hesper is slain instantly (Fortitude DC 15 negates). A hesper can bond with only one reactor at a time, and forming a new bond severs its previous bond.

ECOLOGY

Environment any starship or urban
Organization solitary, pair, or clique (3–12)
Treasure incidental

Hespers are specialized fey are drawn to advanced technology, and especially technological power sources. They see themselves as protectors of this technology, but through their natural curiosity, they also sometimes cause disruption as they reconfigure, rebuild, and rearrange the systems that they take an interest in.

Hespers are somewhat shorter than humans on average but incredibly dense, weighing 300 to 400 pounds despite their lithe builds.

They glow faintly with a radioactive green color. The radiation they emit is magical in nature and not generally dangerous to be around—unless they wish to be.

Hespers are naturally curious in all things and filled with boundless energy. They rarely pass up an opportunity to interact with new people or new machines, and they ask countless questions, but are rarely patient enough to wait for the answers.
